To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sensitivity analysis for the computational design and optimization of ductile damage in porous materials can be efficiently implemented in a finite element framework, and the developed design techniques can be effectively used for a wide variety of manufacturing problems.

the sensitivity analysis and the optimization of metal forming processes are feasible and can be applied successfully to the design of metal forming dies and to the design of preforms for near net shape processes.
the developed sensitivity-based optimization techniques are effective in the design of metal forming operations for materials with ductility damage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a design framework for the optimal design of forming processes for porous metal parts.
the design of metal forming process parameters for ductile damage and the development of new design tools for the computational design and optimization of forming processes.

the development and implementation of a computational framework for the design of metal forming and casting processes that account for material and process induced anisotropy, and the development of novel design techniques for the design of porous materials and their manufacturing processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the developed design techniques are effective in the design of forming processes for porous and ductile materials.
the computational methods presented in the thesis are effective and accurate, and can be used to design and optimize metal forming processes for a wide range of applications.
the developed design methodology is a powerful and effective tool for the computational design and optimization of forming processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the computational design of deformation processes can be performed in an accurate, efficient and robust manner.
a new design paradigm is introduced for the manufacturing of porous metal parts with a desired porosity distribution.
we are able to predict and control the deformation behavior of porous metal forming components with the help of a gradient based sensitivity design approach.

the computational design of deformation processes is feasible and can lead to significant savings in terms of cost, material and time.

the design of metal forming process is feasible and can be performed efficiently with the proposed sensitivity analysis and optimization techniques.
